newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakh T-bill yields likely to edge down-dealers.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh T-bill yields likely to edge down-dealers.

text.p: Yields on Kazakh three- and six-month Treasury bills are likely to edge down next week because demand for government securities remains high and investors are psychologically prepared for lower yields, traders said on Friday.
Kazakhstan's finance ministry is offering 650 milllion tenge of six-month MKM discount T-bills on Monday and 600 million tenge of three-month paper on Tuesday.
This week, the yield on three-month T-bills fell to 21.72 percent annual from 22.12 percent at the previous auction last Tuesday. Demand was two billion tenge against 500 million tenge on offer.
The yield on six-month paper fell at its last auction on April 14 to 24.52 percent annual from 25.23 percent, with demand of 2.67 billion tenge against 580 million on offer.
Dealers said high demand could further lower yields next week.
"Demand is so much higher than the amount on offer. The government securities market remains attractive because it is not risky," said Yerzham Arynbasarov, from Almaatinsky Torgovo-Finansovy Bank.
Foreign investors, who are entitled to buy 15-30 percent of each T-bill issue are another important facrtor.
"We often feel that foreign investors are very aggressive and a lower yield would suit them," said a trader from state-run Bank TuranAlem.
Other dealers said the markets was psychologically ready to accept lower yields.
"Even the level of 20 percent annual has been passed already," said Baizhan Gabdullin of Alfabank Khazakhstan, adding his bank was already investing in T-bill repo operations at 18 percent.
